ety.text: PIE word *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros From Middle English west, from Old English west, from Proto-West Germanic *westr (“western”), from Proto-Germanic *westrą (“west”), from Proto-Germanic *westraz (“west”), from Proto-Indo-European *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros (“evening”).

senses.d: The direction opposite to that of the earth's rotation, specifically 270°.
ex: We used to live in the west of the country.
Portugal lies to the west of Spain.

senses.d: The western region or area; the inhabitants thereof.
In a church: the direction of the gallery, opposite to the altar, and opposite to the direction faced by the priest when celebrating ad orientem.
ex: The seating for honored persons (clergy) is at the liturgical west, opposite the entrance and lectern.

senses.d: Situated or lying in or toward the west; westward.
Of or pertaining to the west; western.
Designating, or situated in, the liturgical west, that part of a church which is opposite to, and farthest from, the part containing the chancel.
ex: as in the mosaic of the ascension on San Frediano's liturgical west (geographically east) façade.

senses.d: To move to the west; (of the sun), to set.
